evidence.quoted_text:
"manager_restarted": (
            (((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
             .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                 .get("pid") or 0) > 0
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("pid")
            and bool(((manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and bool(((manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager") or {})
                     .get("invocation_id"))
            and (manager.get("before") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")
            != (manager.get("after") or {}).get("manager", {}).get("invocation_id")),
evidence.reason: The `manager_restarted` check treats any manager PID/invocation-ID change as proof of an isolated restart, but it never verifies that the before/after manager snapshots are from the same boot. The same snapshot shape carries `boot_id` for the reboot check, so a guest reboot between the two manager inspections can also change the manager PID and invocation ID and falsely satisfy `manager_restarted` even though the observations span a reboot. Requiring nonempty equal manager-snapshot boot IDs, while keeping the existing PID and invocation-ID checks, is a small correctness fix within the existing intended behavior.
